title: EvoSyn: Generalizable Evolutionary Data Synthesis for Verifiable Learning

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary optimization of data-filtering strategies for synthesizing executable, verifiable training data
mechanism.populationDetail: The implementation explicitly combines MAP-Elites with island-based population models, but island count, migration, and concrete population layout are not reported.
mechanism.archiveDetail: MAP-Elites is combined with user-defined feature dimensions to maintain diversity; exact descriptors and archive admission/eviction rules are unspecified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper names both island-based population models and MAP-Elites but gives no concrete population/archive update algorithm.
mechanism.generationDetail: The paper says an initial filtering strategy is iteratively improved but does not describe whether each new strategy edits a selected parent, is generated from scratch, or fuses multiple parents.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Per-seed-instance criterion checks are aggregated into one consistency score; the paper explicitly says the aggregate guides later evolution but does not say per-instance outcomes are retained or exposed to the LLM.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Although search starts from an initial strategy, no later parent sampling source, number, or rule is specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The evolved object is an executable scoring/filtering function over sets of candidate solutions and tests, rather than an ordinary task solution artifact.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/EVOSYN GENERALIZABLE EVOLUTIONARY DATA SYNTHESIS FOR VERIFIABLE LEARNING.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey cites EvoSyn for QD, metadata, and application context. QD is directly supported. Metadata is plausible as per-instance checks, but the paper only explicitly says the aggregate score guides evolution; qualify any claim that raw checks are preserved/reused. Add island-population and implicit explore/exploit coverage. The generation prompt and parent-offspring protocol are not disclosed; the suggested candidate-prompt placement captures its existence only.
